Hi @kofi, regarding your question about parse_amount edge cases from the design review: Commas are only accepted in real thousands positions. The first group must have 1-3 digits and every following group exactly 3 digits. So "1,234,567.00" is valid, but "1,23.00" or "12,3456" (European format) must raise ValueError.

Hi @lena, regarding your question about round_div edge cases: the design review notes state that 'half_up' is symmetric around zero, meaning a negative exact half is rounded away from zero (e.g., round_div(-5, 2) == -3). This ensures refunds and credit notes round to exactly the negation of the matching charge.
Sure! Design decision: when last_number belongs to an earlier year than the target year, next number is CN-<year>-0001. E.g. after CN-2024-0173, first of 2025 is CN-2025-0001.

Hey @omar, regarding LEDGERLIB-105: The design decision was that within one day, credits (positive amounts) are posted before debits (negative amounts). Within each group (credits/debits), transactions keep their input order. So for your test: payout (7000, credit) comes first, then rent (-5000) and fees (-1000) as debits in their original input order. Hope that helps!
